tools.name: book2skill
tools.does: Books or manuals you own, or public-domain texts, into a tested Agent Skill, one stage per call (extract, split, index, build, audit, eval, refresh, export) with a receipt per stage and an eval gate of 0.6 that refuses export; pass local files, not URLs

args.name: stage
args.does: extract | split | index | build | audit | eval | refresh | export

args.name: src
args.does: extract: the source file you own (PDF, EPUB, DOCX, MD, TXT)

args.name: work
args.does: work dir, e.g. work/mybook (every stage except audit)

args.name: skill
args.does: skill dir, e.g. skills/mybook (build, audit, eval, export)

args.name: name
args.does: build: skill name, a-z0-9- and equal to the skill dir name

args.name: description
args.does: build: what the skill does and when to use it

args.name: qa
args.does: eval: the question file, e.g. evals/mybook_qa.jsonl

args.name: out
args.does: extract: the work dir to write; export: the output dir

for: autonomous-factory: packs for sale (skillworks finish bar S3)
Maxim's job work: a manual or doc into a tested skill
center skill doctor (skillworks bars S1, S2)

tools.name: part_score
tools.does: One live line per part of skillworks (P1 pipeline, P2 MCP server, P3 seeds, P4 eval gate, P5 shop, workspace) from receipts, eval rates and a local MCP handshake; read-only, no arguments
for: center kernel Grow rule 'Parts' (is skillworks getting better)

tools.name: cron_skip_clean
tools.does: Skip a run when nothing changed: fingerprints a directory, prints SKIP clean <id> when it matches the state file, else writes the state JSON and prints RUN <id>; no network

args.name: state
args.does: state file to read and write (JSON), e.g. state/watch.json

for: every loop repo: skip the round when the inputs did not change (saves tokens)

tools.name: pipe_dry_run
tools.does: Plan a batch before spending: reads every .txt in a directory, estimates tokens (chars // 4 each) against a cap and prints DRY-RUN <n> items spend <t> tokens (cap <c>); writes nothing

args.name: out
args.does: output directory the real run would use (not created in a dry run)

args.name: cap
args.does: maximum tokens of spend, an integer

for: factory batch runs: know the cost before a run
